A 58-year-old male seeks medical attention for dark stools and dyspnea of 3 days' duration. He
describes epigastric discomfort occurring 1-3 hours post-meals, particularly with spicy foods, for the
past 3 months. He reports a 5-pound weight loss and decreased appetite. His history includes a recent
trip to the Dominican Republic 6 months ago, a 5-pack-year smoking history (recently quit), tension
headaches, and irritable bowel syndrome. He takes ibuprofen and probiotics. Physical examination
reveals: temperature 98.0°F (36.6°C), blood pressure 111/79 mmHg, pulse 78/min, respirations
12/min, conjunctival pallor, and epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding. Laboratory findings
show: - Hemoglobin: 7.2 g/dL - Platelets: 176,000/mm^3 - Positive heme occult stool test - Leukocyte
count: 11,000/mm^3 - Segmented neutrophils: 56% - Bands: 2% - Eosinophils: 1% - Basophils: 0.8% -
Lymphocytes: 35% - Monocytes: 5% Endoscopy reveals diffuse gastric mucosal erythema and a 1 cm
lesion with a smooth, flat base in the proximal duodenum. What is the most likely mechanism
responsible for these endoscopic findings? Answer Choices: (A) H. pylori-induced cytotoxin-associated
gene A (CagA) activity (B) Overuse of antacids leading to rebound hyperacidity (C) Impaired
bicarbonate secretion in the duodenum (D) Urease production (E) Reduced prostaglandin synthesis (F)
Decreased mucosal blood flow due to smoking (G) Direct mucosal injury from nonsteroidal

anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) (H) Gastrin-secreting tumor (I) Increased gastrin secretion due to
Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (J) Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition
 A. Urease production
B. Gastrin-secreting tumor
C. Impaired bicarbonate secretion in the duodenum
D. H. pylori-induced cytotoxin-associated gene A (CagA) activity
E. Direct mucosal injury from nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
F. Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition
G. Decreased mucosal blood flow due to smoking
H. Overuse of antacids leading to rebound hyperacidity
I. Increased gastrin secretion due to Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
J. Reduced prostaglandin synthesis
